instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and stir in the 1 tsp salt.
Juice the 3 limes into a large bowl. That should be about 5 tbsp. Stir in the fish sauce and sugar until the sugar dissolves. Taste it. It should be quite sour, with some salt and a little sweetness.
Thinly slice the shallot. Trim the lemongrass, peel off the tough outer layers, slice the bottom 4 inches very thin and chop it fine. Chop 1 cup of cilantro leaves and 1/2 cup of mint leaves.
Take the pot off the heat and add the shrimp. Poach them for 2 to 3 minutes, until they are pink and just cooked through. Don't let them go longer or they turn rubbery.
Lift the shrimp out with a slotted spoon and transfer them into the dressing while they're still warm. Toss to coat.
Bring the same water back to a boil. Add the noodles and cook them for 3 to 4 minutes, or as the package says. Drain, rinse under cold water and divide among four bowls.
Add the shallot, lemongrass, cilantro and mint to the shrimp and toss again. Taste it. If it's flat, add a splash more fish sauce.
Spoon the shrimp salad and its dressing over the noodles. Serve with the chili garlic sauce on the table for anyone who wants heat.
method_notes: The Thai shrimp salad sold as pla goong or yum goong is the same dish: shrimp poached for a couple of minutes and tossed warm in a lime, fish sauce and sugar dressing, with shallot and herbs. Simply Suwanee leads (4.9 from 14 votes, called Pla Goong) and serves it with jasmine rice or rice noodles; Hungry in Thailand adds lemongrass, and Recipezazz, which names the dish Yum Goong, poaches the shrimp in lemongrass water. Changed for the list: the peanuts are left out to keep it nut-free, the chili paste moves to the table, and rice noodles cook in the poaching water to keep it quick. Under 20 ratings, so this is a fallback lead.
